title: The Call of Abraham, part 4 of 5: Sarai, Hagar and the God who sees
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tents of black goat hair, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAM.name: Abram
ABRAM.desc: Abram, a tall, strong, upright man who looks about sixty, with warm brown weathered skin, thick wavy dark hair heavily streaked with grey reaching his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAI.name: Sarai
SARAI.desc: Sarai, a strikingly beautiful, graceful woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy black hair with a few silver threads, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

HAGAR.name: Hagar
HAGAR.desc: Hagar, a slender young Egyptian woman of about twenty-five, with reddish-brown skin, large dark almond-shaped eyes, a narrow face with a small pointed chin, and straight black hair cut level at the shoulders with a straight fringe across her forehead, wearing no head shawl, in an ankle-length long-sleeved servant's dress of plain sand-brown wool tied at the waist with a narrow faded green cloth sash, a thin copper bracelet on her left wrist, and simple leather sandals

blocks.ONE: Exactly one person in the picture, no one else
blocks.TWO: Exactly two people in the picture, one man and one woman, no one else
blocks.NOLIGHTFIG: No figure, no face and no human shape in the light
blocks.HANDS: Only hands and forearms are in the frame, no faces
blocks.EMPTY: A pure landscape with no human being in it: not one person, figure or silhouette anywhere, near or far
blocks.TENT: a low, wide tent of black goat-hair cloth stretched over wooden poles and held by ropes and wooden pegs
blocks.SERVANTS: herdsmen and serving women in knee-length tunics and ankle-length dresses of rough wool in undyed cream, brown and grey, the women with plain head shawls
blocks.CANAAN: the hill country of Canaan: rolling limestone hills with grey rock ledges, spring grass, wild flowers, scattered olive trees and thickets of evergreen oak
blocks.OAK: an enormous, ancient oak tree with a massive gnarled trunk and a broad, spreading crown of dark green leaves
blocks.NEGEV: the Negev: a dry southern land of pale stony hills, dusty gullies and sparse grey thorn scrub under a hard blue sky
blocks.INTENT: inside a tent of black goat-hair cloth at night, with wooden poles, woven rugs on the ground, a sleeping mat and one small clay oil lamp burning with a single flame
blocks.STARS: an immense, clear night sky crowded from edge to edge with thousands upon thousands of sharp bright stars and the pale band of the Milky Way; no moon, no clouds, no shooting stars, no comets
blocks.NOHALO: No halo, no rays and no glow around any person
blocks.VISION: Painted as a dim vision seen in sleep: all the people are small dark silhouettes without faces, seen against a smoky amber glow, and the edges of the picture are lost in deep darkness
blocks.MAPLOOK: A painted bird's-eye landscape seen from very high above, like an old oil-painted map with nothing written on it: no letters, no words, no labels, no symbols, no compass rose and no border
blocks.TWOWOMEN: Exactly two people in the picture, both of them women, no one else: no man anywhere
blocks.THREE: Exactly three people in the picture: one man and two women, no one else
blocks.CAMP: Abram's camp: several low, wide tents of black goat-hair cloth pitched in the shade of enormous ancient oak trees with massive trunks, in a green valley among limestone hills
blocks.PREGNANT: she is with child, and her belly is clearly rounded under her sand-brown dress
blocks.SHUR: the desert on the road to Shur: a wide, empty wilderness of pale sand, gravel flats and low bare tawny ridges under a vast sky, with one faint beaten track running across it toward the horizon
blocks.SPRING: a small desert spring: clear water welling up from under a ledge of pale rock into a shallow pool a few paces wide, ringed with green rushes and shaded by one small tamarisk tree, the only green in the bare desert
blocks.NEARLIGHT: a strong, soft white-gold light shines across the scene from just outside the right-hand edge of the picture, low and level, as from a bright presence standing there unseen; the source of the light is outside the picture
blocks.NOANGEL: The light is formless light only: no figure, no face, no body, no wings and no human shape anywhere in the light or in the picture's bright side
blocks.WELL: a desert well: a low ring of rough piled stones about knee high around a dark round shaft, with a worn stone trough beside it
blocks.NOSTRIKE: No one strikes anyone: no whip, no rod, no stick and no raised hand
blocks.BABY: a newborn baby boy with warm reddish-brown skin and a little soft black hair, wrapped tightly in plain undyed cream wool swaddling cloth so that only his small sleeping face shows
blocks.DUSTY: her dress and her bare forearms are grey with road dust and her hair is tangled by the wind
blocks.NOEGYPT: No pyramids, no sphinx, no obelisks, no statues and no writing anywhere

segs.text: Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram,
Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.
And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
And he slept with Hagar, and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
Then Sarai said to Abram,
May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.
Here,
said Abram,
your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.
Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert—the spring along the road to Shur.
Hagar, servant of Sarai,
he said,
where have you come from, and where are you going?
I am running away from my mistress Sarai,
she replied.
So the angel of the LORD told her,
Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.
Then the angel added,
I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.
The angel of the LORD proceeded:
Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
He will be a wild donkey of a man, and his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.
So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her:
You are the God who sees me,
for she said,
Here I have seen the One who sees me!
Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.

stills.prompt: Character reference sheet of {HAGAR}: a full-body front view standing and a head-and-shoulders portrait, side by side, calm expression, plain warm-grey background. One person only, shown twice. No tools, no jar, empty hands. She is slim and is not with child. The plain warm-grey painted background fills the whole picture from edge to edge behind both views: no landscape, no sky, no ground plants, no buildings, no writing and no other people anywhere. The skin is the same reddish-brown in both views.

Early morning in {CAMP}. Small in the middle distance a few {SERVANTS}, are at work: one woman milks a goat, one man leads sheep out to graze, and thin blue smoke lies low over one cooking fire. No children anywhere. Wide view.

Sarai had borne him no children: {SARAI}, sits alone on a woven rug in the open doorway of {TENT}, a wooden hand spindle lying idle in her lap, her empty hands resting on it, looking away into the distance with a quiet sadness. There is no child, no cradle and no toy anywhere. {ONE}. Medium view.

An Egyptian maidservant named Hagar: {HAGAR}, walks toward the viewer between black goat-hair tents in morning light, carrying a large clay water jar on her left shoulder and steadying it with one hand, her eyes lowered. She is slim and is not with child. {ONE}. Medium view.

So Sarai said to Abram: {INTENT}, two people sit facing each other on the rugs. On the left {SARAI}, leans forward speaking earnestly with one open hand held out; on the right {ABRAM}, sits listening with his hands on his knees. {TWO}. Medium view.

The LORD has prevented me from bearing children: close view of the face of {SARAI}, by the warm light of one small oil lamp at night, speaking with pain in her eyes, her brows drawn together, a tear standing in one eye. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Please go to my maidservant: in the evening outside the tents, {HAGAR}, kneels alone on the ground beside a small cooking fire, grinding grain by pushing a rounded stone back and forth on a flat grinding stone, unaware that anyone is speaking of her. Behind her a black goat-hair tent glows faintly with lamplight from inside. She is slim and is not with child. {ONE}. Medium view.

And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai: close view of the face of {ABRAM}, by the warm light of one small oil lamp at night, his eyes lowered, in the act of giving one slow, grave nod. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar: in daylight between the black goat-hair tents, two women walk toward the viewer. On the left {SARAI}, walks half a step ahead, leading the other by the wrist with a set, resolved face; on the right {HAGAR}, follows with her head bowed and her eyes on the ground. Hagar is slim and is not with child. {TWOWOMEN}. Medium view.

And gave her to Abram to be his wife: three people stand before the open doorway of {TENT}, under an oak. From left to right they are: {HAGAR}, standing with her head bowed; {SARAI}, in the middle, who holds Hagar's hand and lays it in Abram's open hand; and {ABRAM}, on the right, receiving her hand with a grave face. {THREE}. Hagar is slim and is not with child. Medium view.

{SARAI}, walks away alone from the tent toward the viewer in the low light of evening, her arms folded tightly across her body, her face turned a little aside, composed and stiff. Behind her, out of focus, the closed black goat-hair tent under the oak. {ONE}. Medium close view.

{EMPTY}. Night in the camp: one low, wide tent of black goat-hair cloth with its door flap closed, a faint warm glow of lamplight showing along the bottom edge of the cloth, under the dark crown of an enormous oak, with {STARS}, above. Nothing inside the tent is seen. Wide view.

When Hagar realized that she was pregnant: {HAGAR}, stands alone beside a tent pole in early morning light, looking down at herself in dawning wonder, both her hands laid flat on her belly; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. Medium close view from the knees up.

She began to despise her mistress: before a black goat-hair tent in daylight, two women. On the left, standing tall, {HAGAR}, looks down sidelong at the other woman with her chin lifted and a cold, scornful face, one hand resting on her rounded belly; {PREGNANT}. On the right {SARAI}, kneels on the ground kneading dough in a wooden trough and looks up at her, stung. {TWOWOMEN}. Medium view.
Close view of the face of {HAGAR}, in daylight, her chin lifted and her head turned a little aside, looking down past her shoulder with a small, cold, scornful smile. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

May the wrong done to me be upon you: under {OAK}, in daylight, two people stand facing each other. On the left {SARAI}, angry, points straight at the man's chest with one hand; on the right {ABRAM}, has stepped back half a pace with both his open hands lifted a little in surprise. {TWO}. Medium view.

I delivered my servant into your arms: close view of the face of {SARAI}, in daylight under oak leaves, angry and hurt, her eyes bright with tears, her mouth open in bitter speech. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

She has treated me with contempt: in the foreground {HAGAR}, walks toward the viewer past the tents with a clay water jar on her shoulder, her chin high and her eyes fixed straight ahead, one hand under her rounded belly; {PREGNANT}. Behind her, small in the doorway of a black goat-hair tent, {SARAI}, stands watching her go. {TWOWOMEN}. Medium-wide view.

May the LORD judge between you and me: under {OAK}, {SARAI}, on the left, stands with one hand lifted, palm open, toward the sky and her face turned up; on the right {ABRAM}, stands with his head bowed and his hands hanging at his sides. Bright sky shows through the oak leaves. {TWO}. {NOHALO}. Medium-wide view.

Your servant is in your hands: before {TENT}, {ABRAM}, on the left, holds out both open, empty hands toward the woman, palms up, giving the matter over to her, his face tired; on the right {SARAI}, stands with her arms folded, looking at him. {TWO}. Medium view.

Then Sarai treated Hagar harshly: beside the tents in hot midday light, two women. On the left {SARAI}, stands over the other with a hard face, pointing down with a straight arm at a tall heap of grain and a flat grinding stone. On the right {HAGAR}, kneels at the grinding stone, bent and weary, pushing the rounded stone with both hands, sweat on her face; {PREGNANT}. {TWOWOMEN}. {NOSTRIKE}. Medium view.

{HAGAR}, sits alone at night on the ground behind a black goat-hair tent, her back against a tent pole, her knees drawn up, crying silently with one hand over her mouth and the other on her rounded belly; {PREGNANT}. Dim blue starlight, a far glow of embers. {ONE}. Medium view.

She fled from her: in the grey light before dawn, {HAGAR}, hurries away from the camp toward the viewer, a small leather water skin slung over her shoulder and a cloth bundle held to her chest, glancing back over her shoulder at the dark sleeping tents under the oaks behind her; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. No one follows her. Medium view.

Seen from behind and far off, one small lone woman in a sand-brown dress with shoulder-length black hair walks away from us, southward, along a faint track through {NEGEV}. She is tiny in the wide land and carries a small bundle. Exactly one person, seen only from behind, no one else and no animals. Very wide view.
{EMPTY}. A spring of water in the desert, on the road to Shur: {SHUR}. Beside the track in the middle distance lies {SPRING}. Late afternoon light, long shadows. No animals. Wide view.

{HAGAR}, kneels alone at the edge of {SPRING}, bending low to drink clear water from her two cupped hands, worn out; {DUSTY}; {PREGNANT}. Her small bundle lies on the rock beside her. Bare pale desert behind. {ONE}. Medium view.

The angel of the LORD found Hagar by the spring: {HAGAR}, kneeling at the edge of {SPRING}, has turned her head sharply toward the right, startled, one wet hand lifted from the water, because {NEARLIGHT}. The light falls bright on her face, on the rushes and on the water. {DUSTY}; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}. Medium-wide view.

Hagar, servant of Sarai: close view of the face of {HAGAR}, lit from the right by a strong, soft white-gold light whose source is outside the picture, her eyes wide and natural, her lips parted in amazement at hearing her own name, one hand raised beside her brow to shade her eyes. Her hair is tangled and dusty. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}.

{EMPTY}. Where have you come from, and where are you going: a view straight along a faint beaten track that runs from the foreground away across {SHUR}, to the far horizon; in the dust of the foreground one line of small footprints of a single walker leads along the track toward us. No animals. Wide low view.

I am running away from my mistress Sarai: {HAGAR}, kneels on the rock beside {SPRING}, facing toward the right, her head bowed and both her hands pressed flat on her knees, answering plainly; {NEARLIGHT}. {DUSTY}; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}. Medium view.

Return to your mistress: {HAGAR}, kneeling beside {SPRING}, has turned her head to look back over her left shoulder toward the far northern horizon, the way she came, with a face full of dread; a strong, soft white-gold light from outside the right-hand edge of the picture lights her back and shoulder. {DUSTY}; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}. Medium view.

{EMPTY}. Far off, small in a green valley among limestone hills at dusk, stand several low black goat-hair tents under enormous oak trees, with the tiny red spark of one fire among them: the camp she fled. Seen from a distant hilltop. No animals near. Very wide view.

I will greatly multiply your offspring: {HAGAR}, kneeling beside the rushes of a desert spring, looks down in wonder at her own rounded belly, on which both her hands rest; {PREGNANT}. A strong, soft white-gold light from outside the right-hand edge of the picture lights her hands and face. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}. Medium close view.

Too numerous to count: {VISION}. An enormous encampment of countless small black tents spreads over a wide desert plain from the foreground to the far horizon, thousands of them, with countless tiny dark figures of people, camels and flocks moving among them, far too many to count.

You have conceived and will bear a son: close view of the face of {HAGAR}, lit from the right by a strong, soft white-gold light whose source is outside the picture, tears running down her dusty cheeks, her lips parted, her eyes natural and full of astonished hope. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}.

You shall name him Ishmael: very close view of a young woman's two reddish-brown hands, a thin copper bracelet on the left wrist, resting gently and protectively on her rounded belly under a sand-brown wool dress with a faded green sash, lit warmly from the right by white-gold light. {HANDS}.

The LORD has heard your cry of affliction: at night in the open desert, {HAGAR}, kneels alone on the bare stony ground with her face lifted to the sky and her mouth open, crying out in misery, both arms wrapped around herself; {PREGNANT}. Above her, {STARS}. Deep blue starlight. {ONE}. Wide view with the figure small under the great sky.

{EMPTY}. No tents, no camp, no buildings and no man-made thing anywhere. A wild donkey: in the middle of an empty desert gravel plain, far from any dwelling, one wild donkey of the desert, a lean, strong, sandy-brown wild ass with a pale belly, a short dark upright mane and a dark stripe along its back, gallops free with dust flying from its hooves, its head high. It wears no rope, no halter, no bridle and no load. It is the only living creature in the picture. Bare tawny ridges behind. Medium-wide view.

His hand will be against everyone, and everyone's hand against him: {VISION}. On the left, alone on a rocky desert ridge, stands the dark silhouette of one man holding a bow at his side; across a dry ravine, on the right, stands a line of many dark silhouettes of men with spears held upright, facing him. No one shoots, no one strikes and no one falls.

He will live in hostility toward all his brothers: {VISION}. In the foreground on a desert rise stand three small black tents by themselves, with the dark silhouette of one man standing before them with his arms folded, looking out; far away across an empty plain glow the fires of a great cluster of many other tents, apart from him.

So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: beside {SPRING}, {HAGAR}, bows low on her knees toward the right with her forehead almost to the ground and both hands spread on the rock before her; {NEARLIGHT}. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}. Medium-wide view.

You are the God who sees me: close view of the face of {HAGAR}, lifted and turned toward a strong, soft white-gold light that comes from outside the right-hand edge of the picture, her dusty cheeks wet with tears, her eyes natural and wide open, her mouth open in a glad cry of wonder. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOANGEL}.

Here I have seen the One who sees me: beside {SPRING}, in the warm ordinary light of sunset, with no other light, {HAGAR}, stands alone looking toward the right at the empty desert, one hand pressed over her heart and the other on her rounded belly, her face quiet and changed; {PREGNANT}. {ONE}. Nothing but empty desert where she looks. Medium-wide view.

Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi: in the same bare desert in a later day, {WELL}, stands beside a small tamarisk tree and a patch of green rushes. One herdsman in a knee-length brown wool tunic and a head cloth hauls up a leather bucket on a rope and pours water into the trough, where a few sheep and goats crowd to drink. Exactly one person. Medium-wide view.

Between Kadesh and Bered: {MAPLOOK}. A wide tawny desert of pale sand, gravel plains and low bare ridges crossed by one faint track; in the very middle of the picture, one tiny spot of green around a glint of water. Nothing else is green. {NOPEOPLE}. No towns, no buildings.

Seen from behind, {HAGAR}, walks away from us down a grassy slope toward several black goat-hair tents under enormous oak trees in a green valley, going back, a small bundle in one hand; {PREGNANT}. We see only her back. Exactly one person in the foreground; a few tiny distant figures among the far tents. Medium-wide view.

And Hagar bore Abram a son: {INTENT}, {HAGAR}, lies propped on cushions on the sleeping mat under a wool blanket, tired and smiling, holding in the crook of her arm {BABY}. She is no longer with child. One woman and one newborn baby, no one else. Medium close view.

Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son: in morning light before the open doorway of {TENT}, {ABRAM}, stands holding up before him in both hands {BABY}, and looks into the child's face as he speaks his name. One man and one newborn baby, no one else. Medium view.

Abram was eighty-six years old: close view of the weathered, deeply lined face of {ABRAM}, in soft morning light, looking down with wet eyes and a slow smile at a swaddled newborn baby held against his chest, of which only the top of the small dark head and the cream wool cloth are seen at the bottom of the frame. Head and shoulders only. One man and one baby, no one else.

{SARAI}, stands alone in the shadow just inside the doorway of a black goat-hair tent, one hand holding the edge of the tent cloth, looking out toward the bright morning outside with a still, unreadable face. Her arms are empty. There is no child with her. Through the doorway behind her are seen only sunlit grass and the trunk and leaves of a great oak tree: no buildings, no walls, no town, no ruins. {ONE}. Medium close view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 16:1–16, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 16:1-16 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, S Sarai (16:2, 16:5), A Abram (16:6, same voice as earlier units), H Hagar (16:8, 16:13), L the angel of the LORD (16:8-12). Voices S and H are first choices nobody has heard; change them freely at assembly.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: ABRAM and SARAI use the sheets and description text of s01e03b word for word. Abram is 85-86 here (16:16) and is painted from the same sheet as at 75 (a vigorous man who looks about sixty); the aged sheet is left for Genesis 17 (99). New in this unit: refs/REF-HAGAR.jpg (key HAGAR), an Egyptian woman of about twenty-five (her age and looks are I; the text says only Egyptian and maidservant). Her skin and hair follow the EGYPTIANS block of s02e01a; she wears a servant's wool dress and no head shawl, so she is never mistaken for Sarai. That she joined the household in Egypt (12:16) is likely but not stated, and is not shown.

The angel of the LORD (16:7-13) is never given a body or a face. He is pictured only as a strong white-gold light that comes from outside the right-hand edge of the frame (block NEARLIGHT), because 16:13 says it was 'the LORD who had spoken to her' and God is never shown with a face. Whether the angel of the LORD is God himself or a messenger distinct from him is disputed and is not resolved on screen. For the same reason his words (L) are set in the voice already used for God (G in earlier units); this is a default that can be changed at assembly. 'Here I have seen the One who sees me' (16:13, BSB main text) is pictured as Hagar looking into that light; what she saw is not shown.

16:2-4: the giving of Hagar to Abram 'to be his wife' is shown as Sarai laying Hagar's hand in Abram's (I; no rite is described). 'He slept with Hagar' is a closed tent at night whose lamp goes out; nothing is shown. C3 (Sarai walking away) is D. Hagar's feelings before 16:4 are not stated and she is painted only with bowed head.

16:4-5: Hagar's contempt is a lifted chin and a turned face (I). 16:6: the text does not say what Sarai's harsh treatment was; it is pictured as heavy work at the grinding stone under a hard word (I), with no blow, rod or whip, and F3 (Hagar crying at night) is D. 16:6 'she fled': she leaves before dawn with a water skin and a bundle (I). F5: she goes south through the Negev, since Shur lies toward Egypt (I).

16:7: the spring is a small desert pool under a rock ledge with rushes and one tamarisk (I). 16:8 H2 (the track and one line of footprints) is D. 16:9 I2 shows the camp at the Oaks of Mamre (13:18) far off (I).

16:10-12: what the angel foretells is painted as dim visions of faceless silhouettes (block VISION, as in s02e01c). 16:12 follows the BSB main text, 'he will live in hostility toward all his brothers' (the footnote reading is not pictured): L3 shows only a few tents standing apart from a greater camp, and L2 a lone man facing many across a ravine; no fighting, no people or nation is named or marked. L1 is a real wild ass of the desert (onager), free of rope or load.
16:11 K3 pictures 'your cry of affliction' as Hagar crying out alone under the stars on her flight (D; the text does not narrate the cry).

16:14: N1 shows the place in later use as a stone-ringed well with an unnamed herdsman (I: the text calls it a spring in 16:7 and a well in 16:14). The sites of Kadesh and especially Bered are uncertain; N2 is an unlabelled desert seen from above with one green spot and neither place is drawn.

16:15: Hagar's return is not narrated; O1 (seen from behind, walking back to the tents) is I from 16:9 and 16:15. The birth is not shown; O2 shows mother and swaddled child afterwards. The infant Ishmael has a description block only (BABY); the first unit that needs him as a boy designs his sheet (Genesis 17 or 21). P2 (Sarai watching from the tent) is D.
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
